data.title: What is the average length of a queue of cars? (2023)
data.author: alexmolas
data.article_summary: 文章讨论了在山路上车辆排队长度的问题。作者最初通过概率推导，假设车辆速度独立同分布，得出每队列的平均车辆数为2。然而，经过模拟实验后，发现实际结果与此不符。模拟显示，平均队列长度约为10.69，且存在极大变异。作者最初的推导基于几何分布，但未考虑到实际情况中的复杂因素，因此得出了错误的结论。模拟结果更符合实际观察，表明队列长度分布广泛，半数队列长度不超过2，但也有长度极大的情况。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：车队长度和队列数量的数学模型及其推论

不同观点：
• Shawabawa3认为，如果根据上述推理，观察到一个有22,849辆车的队列几乎是不可能的。他指出，在10万辆车中总有一辆车是最慢的，当这辆车出现时，它后面的所有车都会排成一个长队。因此，平均而言，预计在后半段会有一个长达5万辆车的队列。

• Dmurray指出，结论似乎是针对错误的问题得出的：这是否是关于队列数量的公式？第一辆车以概率1开始一个队列，第二辆车只有在比第一辆车慢时（概率1/2）才开始一个新队列，第三辆车只有在比前两辆车都慢时（概率1/3）才开始一个新队列，以此类推。总和是1 + 1/2 + 1/3...，这个公式与博客文章末尾的公式一致，但存在一个错位误差。平均队列长度应为车辆总数除以这个调和数列的总和，这个和也会趋于无穷大。

• Cgadski总结了一系列独立同分布的抽样问题，并讨论了在何种情况下会抽到一个比第一次抽样更大的值。他认为，如果从绝对连续的分布中抽样，那么这个变量N会具有几何分布的特性，且其期望值为无穷大。他还提到，如果考虑有限时间内形成队列的情况，那么只有当车的速度比队列前车速度快ε时，才会加入该队列，这样就可以避免λ趋近于0的极端情况。此外，他还讨论了“体验”队列长度的问题，指出通过大量数值模拟可以发现，几乎所有司机都会遇到极大的队列。

补充讨论：
• Alexchamberlain以讽刺的方式指出，假设道路只有一个入口、没有出口，并且无限长，似乎还忘了假设道路是没有弹性和质量的。这暗示了对模型假设的质疑。

争议焦点：
• 争议的核心在于车队长度的计算方法和假设的合理性。Shawabawa3和Dmurray对计算公式和队列数量的理解存在分歧，而Cgadski则进一步分析了不同分布假设下的结果差异，并指出了模拟与理论推导之间的矛盾。Alexchamberlain则质疑了模型假设的现实性。

44782229.article_content:
Some time ago I was driving on a twisty mountain road, stuck in a slow-moving queue of cars as it was impossible to overtake safely.
Out of boredom, I was wondering how many cars were in the queue, and, more generally, what would be the average length of queues in this road.
Let’s find out!
First, let’s formalize the problem.
Assume that the road has a single entry, no exits, and is infinitely long (poor drivers!).
Furthermore, upon entering the road each vehicle moves forward at a given average speed.
In this scenario, faster vehicles will eventually catch up with the slower ones in front of them, and, since overtakes are not possible, will slow down and queue behind them.
After some time, a “steady state” is reached where several groups of vehicles form, each moving forward at the speed of the slowest vehicle in front of the queue.
The question we want to answer is, therefore: what is the average length of these groups?
The intuitive (but wrong) approach
The first idea I had was rather intuitive, but as it turns out, wrong.
Let the average speeds of the $i$-th vehicle entering the road be $X_i$, and assume that all $X_1\ldots,X_\infty$ are independent and identically distributed (i.i.d.).
Following our assumptions above, a queue of $n$ vehicles will form if $X_1\leq X_2$, and $X_1 \leq X_3$, and $\ldots$, and $X_1\leq X_n$, and $X_1>X_{n+1}$.
Since all variables are i.i.d., we can find the probability of all of these events to be true as the product of the individual probabilities:
\[p(N=n)=\begin{cases}
1 & n \leq 1 \\
\left[\prod_{i=2}^n p(X_i\geq X_1)\right]
p(X_{n+1}<X_1)
& n \geq 2
\end{cases}\]
Some thought before going on with the math should convince you that the final result does not depend on the distributions of the velocities.
Different distributions would affect how quickly queues form, but not their length after an infinite amount of time.
Indeed, since $X_1$ and $X_i$ are i.i.d., the probability that $X_1\leq X_i$ must be $1/2$.
Actually, for this we do not even need independence, but only exchangeability (which is implied by independence, and therefore holds in our case).
In our case, exchangeable random variables have the property that $p(X_1=x,X_i=x’)=p(X_1=x’,X_i=x)$.
This kind of symmetry means that there is no “preferred” ordering of the two velocities, and therefore the probability that one is larger than the other can only be $1/2$ (you can verify this formally by explicitly writing down and solving an integral for that probability).
Since $p(X_1\leq X_i)=1/2$, expanding the equation above gives:
\[p(N=n)=
p(X_{n+1}<X_1)\prod_{i=2}^n p(X_i\geq X_1)
=
\frac{1}{2} \prod_{i=2}^n \frac{1}{2}=\frac{1}{2^{n-1}}\]
Which holds again for $n>1$; For example, there is a probability of $1/2$ that there are at least two cars.
Finally, the expected value of $N$ is computed as
\[\mathbb{E}[N]=\sum_{n=1}^N n\cdot p(N=n)=\sum_{n=1}^N \frac{n}{2^n}=2\]
Therefore, the average number of cars in a queue is 2! Which definitely does not match my experience ;)
To conclude this (wrong, as we are going to see in a minute) solution, note that the derivation above was somewhat pedantic and brute-forced.
With a little bit more insight, one could realize that, assuming the velocities to be i.i.d., the number of vehicles in a queue is a random variable with Geometric distribution.
Each Bernoulli trial corresponds to a new vehicle entering the road and checking whether it is not faster than the queue of cars in front of it.
A Geometric random variable with parameter $p=1/2$ has the same distribution and expectation that we derived above.
Simulation
As I hinted at the beginning, the reasoning above is actually wrong, and I only realized that because I implemented a simulation and found completely different results.
Let’s dive in!

44782229.article_summary: 文章讨论了在山路上车辆排队长度的问题。作者最初通过概率推导，假设车辆速度独立同分布，得出每队列的平均车辆数为2。然而，经过模拟实验后，发现实际结果与此不符。模拟显示，平均队列长度约为10.69，且存在极大变异。作者最初的推导基于几何分布，但未考虑到实际情况中的复杂因素，因此得出了错误的结论。模拟结果更符合实际观察，表明队列长度分布广泛，半数队列长度不超过2，但也有长度极大的情况。
44782229.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：车队长度和队列数量的数学模型及其推论

不同观点：
• Shawabawa3认为，如果根据上述推理，观察到一个有22,849辆车的队列几乎是不可能的。他指出，在10万辆车中总有一辆车是最慢的，当这辆车出现时，它后面的所有车都会排成一个长队。因此，平均而言，预计在后半段会有一个长达5万辆车的队列。

• Dmurray指出，结论似乎是针对错误的问题得出的：这是否是关于队列数量的公式？第一辆车以概率1开始一个队列，第二辆车只有在比第一辆车慢时（概率1/2）才开始一个新队列，第三辆车只有在比前两辆车都慢时（概率1/3）才开始一个新队列，以此类推。总和是1 + 1/2 + 1/3...，这个公式与博客文章末尾的公式一致，但存在一个错位误差。平均队列长度应为车辆总数除以这个调和数列的总和，这个和也会趋于无穷大。

• Cgadski总结了一系列独立同分布的抽样问题，并讨论了在何种情况下会抽到一个比第一次抽样更大的值。他认为，如果从绝对连续的分布中抽样，那么这个变量N会具有几何分布的特性，且其期望值为无穷大。他还提到，如果考虑有限时间内形成队列的情况，那么只有当车的速度比队列前车速度快ε时，才会加入该队列，这样就可以避免λ趋近于0的极端情况。此外，他还讨论了“体验”队列长度的问题，指出通过大量数值模拟可以发现，几乎所有司机都会遇到极大的队列。

补充讨论：
• Alexchamberlain以讽刺的方式指出，假设道路只有一个入口、没有出口，并且无限长，似乎还忘了假设道路是没有弹性和质量的。这暗示了对模型假设的质疑。

争议焦点：
• 争议的核心在于车队长度的计算方法和假设的合理性。Shawabawa3和Dmurray对计算公式和队列数量的理解存在分歧，而Cgadski则进一步分析了不同分布假设下的结果差异，并指出了模拟与理论推导之间的矛盾。Alexchamberlain则质疑了模型假设的现实性。

data.title: How ChatGPT spoiled my semester (2024)
data.author: edent
data.article_summary: 文章讲述了作者在大学工程心理学课程中遭遇的团队合作问题，主要由于组员过度依赖ChatGPT生成内容。在一次为真实客户进行的团队项目中，作者发现组员直接使用ChatGPT生成的文字，甚至包含与项目无关的内容，如区块链等。这些内容不仅格式明显（如字号不同），而且答非所问。作者不反对借鉴ChatGPT，但认为应先评估和理解其输出。然而，组员们不断重复这种行为，导致作者不得不重写大量内容，感到沮丧和缺乏动力。最终，作者认为如果独自完成项目可能会更有趣，但现在却因组员依赖AI而失去兴趣。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：ChatGPT对学生学习的影响以及在学术和工作环境中的使用

不同观点：
• **ChatGPT不是问题根源，学生自身是关键**：[bradley13]认为，ChatGPT并没有毁掉任何东西，问题在于懒惰的学生。他将学生分为两类：一类利用AI支持学习，另一类则用AI代写作业以逃避学习。

• **LLM（如ChatGPT）在回答问题时存在偏差**：[tossandthrow]指出，ChatGPT有时会回答一个与原问题略有不同的问题，导致写作质量不佳。这可能是因为两个概念在潜在语义空间中相近，导致模型错误映射问题。

• **学生注重成绩而非学习，导致使用ChatGPT作弊**：[sudohalt]认为，学生使用ChatGPT是因为他们更关注成绩和毕业，而不是学习。在时间和成绩压力下，学生倾向于作弊以优化他们的结果。

• **问题在于学生对课程的漠不关心，而非ChatGPT**：[skeaker]表示，使用ChatGPT作弊的现象与过去学生在小组项目中敷衍了事类似，问题在于学生对课程的兴趣，而非技术本身。

• **职场中也存在依赖未审查代码的趋势**：[jatins]指出，职场中也有越来越多的人提交未经仔细审查的代码，这与学生依赖ChatGPT完成作业类似。

• **团队沟通不畅导致编辑冲突**：[nlitsme]认为，团队中不充分的沟通会导致成员之间的工作冲突。单方面编辑他人的工作而不进行讨论是不支持团队合作的表现。

• **从负面经验中学习成长**：[michaelchicory]表示，经历过与目标不一致的团队项目可以教会人们在现实世界中找到合适的合作伙伴的重要性。

• **对ChatGPT的抱怨可能源于沟通不足**：[nuthje]建议，在团队中遇到问题时应首先进行沟通，而不是直接抱怨。团队成员可能有个人困难或不同的观点，理解彼此的立场有助于解决问题。

补充讨论：
• **ChatGPT可能替代低质量的人工贡献**：[PeterStuer]回忆过去小组项目中的问题，指出即使没有ChatGPT，部分成员也可能不会做出有效贡献。因此，使用ChatGPT替代这些低质量贡献可能并不更糟。

• **“少工作”作为生活目标的争议**：[self_awareness]认为，一些学生试图以最少的工作量获得更多成果，这种“资源节约”行为在某种程度上可以理解，但将“少工作”作为生活目标可能并不正确。

争议焦点：
• ChatGPT是否是学生作弊的主要原因，还是学生自身的问题。
• ChatGPT在团队项目中替代低质量人工贡献的合理性。
• 在团队合作中如何有效沟通和处理工作冲突。

44820753.article_content:
How ChatGPT spoiled my semester
October 13, 2024
Every semester, I see a bit more ChatGPT being used in classes. This semester, the most obvious occurrences are in my Engineering Psychology classes.
Engineering Psychology is a second major that I’m doing — it’s the study of how humans interact with technology; a bit like UX design.
In one of those classes, we’re doing a group project for a real industry client. In writing the initial proposal for that project, it was clear that a majority of my groupmates were filling in their portions with writing straight from ChatGPT — still in the tell-tale bullet point form:
Look at those subtly different font sizes!
I told a groupmate that I would take over this section, and deleted the work. Just to come back a few hours later and find a newly ChatGPT’d body of work:
Our project has absolutely nothing to do with blockchain or any of the other word-vomit in here.
Some of the sections were written to answer a subtly different question than the one we were supposed to answer. The writing wasn’t even answering the correct question.
I don’t have a problem with taking inspiration from ChatGPT for assignments, I just think that you should at least evaluate and understand what it’s saying before dumping its output onto your collaborators.
Repeatedly in these Engineering Psychology classes — which seem uniquely bullshitable with LLMs — I find myself buried in clearly ChatGPT’d slop produced by my groupmates.
The projects in these classes are often actually quite interesting! But I have no motivation to wade through the river of cheap verbiage and rewrite parts of the project while my groupmates stand on the banks and watch. Why should I be the one person trying to pull yeoman’s work for all of us?
I think I would love these projects if I were doing them alone. But when my groupmates are proxies for $20/month subscriptions, without even particularly imaginative prompts, I lose all motivation.

April 28, 2022

data.author: Stratoscope

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：员工对Windsurf公司收购后工作条件和去留选择的讨论

不同观点：
• burnt-resistor：认为如果不提供有竞争力的薪酬和足够的股权，那么为公司拼命工作是不值得的。强调了工作与回报应该对等，反对在高压时间表下工作却获得很少回报。

• mullingitover：建议员工接受买断。根据其听闻，Windsurf被收购后大部分员工可能会因不需要认证工作而被解雇，所以接受买断比之后被解雇要好。

• flohofwoe：感谢过去工人斗争得来的劳动权利，并对当前工作环境表示不满。暗示对CEO等高层的不满，认为当前社会缺少对过度压榨员工行为的反抗。

• schwentkerr：提出“Windsurf悖论”，反思收购看起来更像是对公司资源的榨取，未详细阐述具体立场但引发对收购后员工处境的思考。

• dyauspitr：质疑每周工作6天、每天14小时的工作制度，认为这样的工作时间几乎占据了所有清醒时间，质疑这种工作安排的合理性。

• villgax：批评公司过度工作员工的文化，认为这种文化反映了公司的失败。支持开放源代码社区的合作模式，认为不需要通过压榨员工来取得成功，讽刺公司最终可能会因过度压榨导致失败。

• jubbs：表示如果自己是Windsurf员工，会立即接受买断，暗示当前的工作条件过于苛刻。

• cjk：支持接受买断，并从招聘经理的角度指出，重视工作与生活平衡的员工往往更有效率和专注力。虽然承认某些情况下需要加班，但反对将过度工作作为公司文化的常态。

补充讨论：
- 争议焦点在于员工是否应该接受买断。一部分人认为收购后员工迟早会被解雇，因此应该接受买断；另一部分人则从工作条件和文化角度出发，认为买断是逃避恶劣工作环境的较好选择。
- 讨论中多次提到工作与生活平衡、工作时长和公司文化等问题，反映出员工对过度工作和缺乏回报的不满。
- 有人提到了开放源代码社区的合作模式，认为这是一种不需要压榨员工也能取得成功的替代方案。

data.title: In Praise of Quitting
data.author: jger15
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对放弃与坚持的不同看法，以及其在成功和生活中的作用。

不同观点：
• [nicbou] 支持反创始人与拼搏文化的观点，强调损失规避（loss aversion）的心理影响。他认为，曾经无法承受损失的人，即使境遇改变，这种心理依然强烈，因此适时放弃有时是必要的。

• [begueradj] 反对过度强调放弃，并以拳击冠军为例，指出成功不仅仅是获得一次机会，而是通过持续的努力和捍卫来建立 legacy（ legacy）。他认为，坚持在某个领域深耕是建立长久成功的关键，而不是频繁转换领域。

• [begueradj] 进一步指出，许多拳击手在退休后重返赛场是因为他们缺乏时间和其他技能去发展新的成功。他认为，成功的多面性并不意味着要频繁放弃，而是要在某个领域内持久努力。

补充讨论：
• [begueradj] 认为大多数人无法在多个领域同时取得成功，因为每个领域的成功都需要大量时间和练习。因此，放弃某些领域并不意味着失败，而是专注于真正擅长的领域。

争议焦点：
• 放弃是否是建立成功和 legacy 的有效策略，还是通过坚持和捍卫已有的成就来实现长久的成功。

• 对损失规避心理的看法不同：[nicbou] 认为损失规避影响深远，而 [begueradj] 则认为通过坚持和深耕可以克服这种心理并取得成功。

• [begueradj] 认为大多数人无法在多个领域同时取得成功，因为每个领域的成功都需要大量时间和练习。因此，放弃某些领域并不意味着失败，而是专注于真正擅长的领域。

争议焦点：
• 放弃是否是建立成功和 legacy 的有效策略，还是通过坚持和捍卫已有的成就来实现长久的成功。

• 对损失规避心理的看法不同：[nicbou] 认为损失规避影响深远，而 [begueradj] 则认为通过坚持和深耕可以克服这种心理并取得成功。

data.article_summary: 文章介绍了被誉为“数学莫扎特”的数学家陶哲轩（Terence Tao）的卓越成就和他因特朗普政府削减高等教育经费而失去资助的经历。陶哲轩是全球最聪明的数学家之一，从小就是数学天才，目前是加州大学洛杉矶分校教授。他在质数和随机数生成等领域的研究对计算机加密和MRI成像技术有重要贡献。尽管他在2006年获得菲尔兹奖，并被《国家地理》称为“天才”，但特朗普政府的经费削减让他对美国STEM研究的未来感到担忧，甚至无法做出长期规划。这使他成为政府削减高等教育经费的受害者之一。

He’s the ‘Mozart’ of Math and Trump Killed His Funding
The latest casualty in the administration’s assault on higher education is a legendary researcher who embodies the best of America.

(Composite / Photos: GettyImages / Shutterstock)
TERENCE TAO MAY BE ONE OF THE SMARTEST human beings on the planet. That’s not an exaggeration.
Now a UCLA professor, Tao has been a mathematics
superstar
for pretty much his entire life, going all the way back to the early 1970s when he was a
2-year-old
with building blocks showing the other kids how to count. He was 7 when he started calculus, 13 when he became the youngest person ever to win the International Mathematical Olympiad, and 19 when he started his Ph.D. at
Princeton
.
Tao’s work on prime numbers has provided crucial insights into random-number generation, which is the way computers produce the (nearly) unpredictable figures that are necessary for cryptography and cybersecurity. His research into the math of imaging has helped to make MRIs faster and smarter.
In 2006 Tao was awarded the
Fields Medal
—math’s equivalent of the Nobel Prize, as anyone who has watched
Good Will Hunting
knows. In 2017,
National Geographic
included Tao in its “Genius” issue
alongside Michelangelo, Darwin, and Einstein. And among his many admirers Tao is known as the “
Mozart of Math
”—a term of affection in a sometimes cutthroat world, where Tao has a reputation for mentoring young, still undiscovered scholars and sharing credit generously.
He is pretty much the platonic model of an intellectual, innovator, and teacher—the best of America, in so many ways. And now he’s a cautionary tale too, because he just lost his funding in the latest wave of Trump administration cuts. It has left him questioning the future of American STEM research, and his place within it.
“A year ago I was absolutely sure I would be staying at UCLA for the foreseeable future,” Tao told me. “But now that there are existential risks . . . I cannot make any long-term predictions.”

data.title: Show HN: I spent 6 years building a ridiculous wooden pixel display
data.author: benholmen
data.article_summary: 本文讲述了作者花费六年时间建造了一个不实用的大型木制像素显示屏，名为"Kilopixel"（由1000个像素组成）。这个项目灵感来源于一些非传统艺术作品和低帧率显示器，旨在创造一个任何人都能通过网站（kilopx.com）进行互动的缓慢显示装置。作者经历了多次尝试，包括使用乒乓球、泡沫球、木球等多种材料作为像素，但都遇到了成本、重量和一致性等问题。最终，作者放弃了球形像素，转向使用立方体像素。整个项目涉及网络应用、物理控制器、定制CNC构建等多个方面，是作者迄今为止最雄心勃勃的项目。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：机械显示项目的分析与改进建议

不同观点：
• fentonc：对该项目表示赞赏，并分享了自己以前制作的类似机械显示项目，该项目通过打孔卡和手摇装置驱动，所有像素同时变化。他强调了机制开发中的相似之处。
• re：对项目表示赞赏，同时提出了几项改进建议，包括在完成提交后将“笔”移开以拍摄完整的图片、在网站上显示当前正在绘制的作品的归属信息、创建历史画廊展示已完成的作品，并提出目前缺少已完成作品的固定链接。
• theletterf：以幽默的方式表达了对项目超低刷新率的喜爱，并引用了“Calm Technology”的概念。
• aarondf：认为该项目可能是他所见过的每像素成本最高的显示项目，但同时也表示这是他最喜欢的项目，以一种“荒谬但美好”的方式呈现。
• xpe：提出了一种技术改进建议，将立方体的一个边朝前，使得每个立方体有两个相邻的暗面和两个相邻的亮面，从而可以同时显示两个图像，一个从左45°观看，另一个从右45°观看。
• GistNoesis：分享了自己用磁 spheres 制作物理显示的实验，并提出通过3D打印和电磁头移动这些磁体以实现图像显示的进一步设想。
• bubblebeard：赞赏项目体现了对探索和学习的热爱，认为项目的过程比结果更重要，并称赞项目的成就。
• TrnsltLife：赞赏项目，并联想到Gibson & Sterling的小说《Difference Engine》中的kinotrope，提到有人用伺服电机制作类似项目，但成本较高。
• fuzzieozzie：提到一个更实际的商业化项目Vestaboard，作为一个参考。
• mappu：提到柏林技术博物馆中有一个全彩的类似显示器，使用12800个立方体，每个立方体有4种颜色。
• derefr：提出了一种使用热敏打印机和卷纸的“显示”设计，作为零功耗的点阵显示方案。
• saltcured：尝试想象“更快”的变体，包括使用重力或气动系统驱动木制球体显示不同颜色，并提出使用旋转块和伺服/电磁系统实现快速图像切换的设想。
• cinntaile：提到一个关于对抗图像的鱼项目，并指出通过训练神经网络解决相关问题。
• joemi：对项目表示赞赏，并提出通过优化提高速度的设想，包括在不需要X轴对齐的情况下完成整列的旋转，并建议制造自动化专家可能能够进一步提升项目效率。

补充讨论：
• 项目的美学和技术细节引起了广泛讨论，包括对超低刷新率的欣赏和对高成本的调侃。
• 多个评论者提出了技术改进建议，涉及显示机制、图像排列和速度优化等方面。
• 一些评论者分享了相关的项目和参考资料，扩展了讨论的范围。
• 争议焦点在于项目的实用性和成本，但总体上评论者对项目的创新性和艺术价值表示肯定。

44787902.article_content:
I spent 6 years building a ridiculous wooden pixel display
August 2, 2025
TL,DR: I built the world's most impractical 1000-pixel display and anyone in the world can draw on it
If you just want to play with it, goto
kilopx.com
.
The backstory
Six years ago I had an idea to build a large, inefficient display with a web interface that anyone could interact with. I've enjoyed
Danny Rozin's unconvenional mirrors
over the years and was inspired by an
eInk movie player that played at 24 frames per
hour
that got me thinking about a laborious display that could slowly assemble an image.
I landed on the idea of a 40Ã25 pixel grid of pixels, turned one by one by a single mechanism. Compared to our modern displays with millions of pixels changing 60 times a second, a wooden display that changes a single pixel 10 times a
minute
is an incredibly inefficient way to create an image. Conveniently, 40Ã25 = 1,000 pixels, leading to the name
Kilopixel
and the six-letter domain name
kilopx.com
. How do you back down from that? That's the best domain name I've ever owned.
So I got to work. This project has everything: a web app, a physical controller, a custom CNC build, generated gcode, tons of fabrication, 3d modeling, 3d printing, material sourcing - so much to get lost in. It's the most ambitious project I've ever built.
The first prototype: 21Ã3 pixels
My first thought was to use a wooden gantry that would ride on some sort of track. Since I'm most comfortable working with wood, it's my default prototyping medium. However, I quickly pivoted to extruded aluminum and the excellent
hardware kits from Openbuilds
that include pulleys, gantry parts, extruded aluminum, and timing belts. It's very similar to the materials used in 3D printer frames, and connects very easily with off the shelf stepper motors. This allowed me to build a gantry with X and Y, essentially a wall-mounted XY plotter. I built the first prototype with two stepper motors, a Raspberry Pi, a CNC controller, and a beefy power supply. It allowed me to generating and sending instructions to the CNC controller to move to a particular pixel, turning that pixel, and reading values from sensors. It also revealed quite a few problems with my pixel choices and pixel manipulation mechanisms.
1,000 of anything is
expensive
Picking pixels was a real adventure. I've tried ping pong balls, styrofoam balls, bouncy balls, wooden balls, 3d printed balls, golf balls, foam balls...anything approximately spherical and about 1-1.5in in diameter. The problems I encountered were largely cost (even a 50Â¢ ball is $500 of balls), weight (again, a thousand of these things), and availability. For a long time I thought ping pong balls were my best bet, so I purchased a few hundred of them, 3d printed painting jigs, and spray painted them. I used a hot nail to melt two opposite holes on each ball so they could be strung up on the display.
Ping pong balls are basically soda cans
You can stand on a soda can,
as long as it's not open
. Open the can, and it crushes easily. Ping pong balls are the same way. They're relatively strong until you melt two holes in them. Then they can be deformed, which is fatal to any spray paint you've put on them. And not only are they fragile, but the cheap ones are inconsistently sized, and a half millimeter here and there adds up when you have a row of 40 balls. Ping pong balls were a no-go.
Nerfed
My next attempt at a cheap, spherical pixel was foam Nerf balls - much smaller than ping pong balls, and only available in bright colors. They accepted spray paint OK but the paint deteriorated over time.
It was difficult to consistently bore a hole through the nerf balls, and they really liked to grab the wire and were hard to turn. I struggled to consistently turn them and I wasn't thrilled with the bright colors.
I also tried bouncy balls (hard to drill a hole, hard to paint, inconsistent sizes, heavy), wooden balls (not very round, hard to paint a crisp line, heavy), and styrofoam balls (hard to paint with acrylic paint, and they melt with spray paint).
Turning balls
I had the idea to use a small, slow motor to rotate a LEGO wheel against the ping pong ball. I'd use a reflectivity sensor to detect if it was showing black or white, and stop once the pixel was rotated properly. I modeled and printed a custom hub for a LEGO wheel, a few different mechanisms to move the wheel in and out of contact of the sphere, and an interface for the gantry. I tried using a solenoid to push the motor into the ball, which was underpowered, and a servo. Neither approach worked great and ultimately I decided this ball turning approach was a dead end.
Pivoting to non-spherical pixels
In 2024 I had a couple of productive conversations with
Joe Tannenbaum on the Side Project podcast
and
Chris Morrell on the Over Engineered podcast
. Those conversations helped me consider that maybe balls were not the way to go - I thought about flaps and illuminated buttons, then settled on a cubic

• TrnsltLife：赞赏项目，并联想到Gibson & Sterling的小说《Difference Engine》中的kinotrope，提到有人用伺服电机制作类似项目，但成本较高。
• fuzzieozzie：提到一个更实际的商业化项目Vestaboard，作为一个参考。
• mappu：提到柏林技术博物馆中有一个全彩的类似显示器，使用12800个立方体，每个立方体有4种颜色。
• derefr：提出了一种使用热敏打印机和卷纸的“显示”设计，作为零功耗的点阵显示方案。
• saltcured：尝试想象“更快”的变体，包括使用重力或气动系统驱动木制球体显示不同颜色，并提出使用旋转块和伺服/电磁系统实现快速图像切换的设想。
• cinntaile：提到一个关于对抗图像的鱼项目，并指出通过训练神经网络解决相关问题。
• joemi：对项目表示赞赏，并提出通过优化提高速度的设想，包括在不需要X轴对齐的情况下完成整列的旋转，并建议制造自动化专家可能能够进一步提升项目效率。

补充讨论：
• 项目的美学和技术细节引起了广泛讨论，包括对超低刷新率的欣赏和对高成本的调侃。
• 多个评论者提出了技术改进建议，涉及显示机制、图像排列和速度优化等方面。
• 一些评论者分享了相关的项目和参考资料，扩展了讨论的范围。
• 争议焦点在于项目的实用性和成本，但总体上评论者对项目的创新性和艺术价值表示肯定。

data.title: Herbie detects inaccurate expressions and finds more accurate replacements
data.author: bwidlar
data.article_summary: Herbie是一款自动提升浮点运算精度的工具，能够检测不准确的表达式并找到更精确的替代方案。例如，将不准确的$\sqrt{x+1} - \sqrt{x}$替换为更准确的$\frac{1}{\sqrt{x+1} + \sqrt{x}}$。Herbie通过网页演示、教程和文档帮助用户了解和使用其功能。它还定期发布更新，如Herbie 2.2引入了新的平台API，Herbie 2.0优化了速度和精度等。Herbie项目还涉及与其他工具的整合和学术研究，如FPBench和Herbgrind。此外，Herbie团队积极参与各类学术会议和讲座，推广该工具并分享研究成果。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Herbie工具的现状及其潜在发展方向，包括其在编译器中的集成以及在具体应用场景中的使用。

不同观点：
• tialaramex认为Herbie目前的功能很优秀，但更重要的洞见是将这种工具集成到编译器中的可能性。他设想未来的编程语言可以直接让开发者指定表达式的近似值，并给出精度和性能参数，类似于正则表达式的处理方式。
• RossBencina对tialaramex的观点表示感兴趣，但提到之前多次讨论中有人指出该工具在某些情况下表现不佳，并询问Herbie最近的更新情况。
• russfink提出了一个具体的技术问题，询问为什么表达式sqrt(x+1) - sqrt(x)对于所有x>1是不准确的，以及为什么1/(…)更好。
• TheFuzzball幽默地表示希望Herbie不要再出现问题（可能指之前的bug或不稳定表现）。
• ashirviskas好奇这种工具是否能帮助优化AI推理和训练引擎，或者这些引擎是否已经被优化到极致，并提到llama.cpp可能是一个很好的应用目标。
• 4gotunameagain称赞Herbie工具很棒，并分享了自己在使用Herbie进行长时间模拟以减少累积误差的经验。
• permalaise表示对Herbie的工作感到印象深刻，认为其具有价值。

补充讨论：
• 关于Herbie在编译器中的潜在集成以及其未来发展方向的讨论是一个重要议题，涉及到编程语言设计和浮点运算处理的简化。
• 对Herbie的具体技术问题（如russfink的问题）表明社区对工具的细节和数学原理仍有疑问。
• 一些评论（如TheFuzzball和RossBencina）提到了Herbie的稳定性和更新情况，显示出对工具可靠性和持续发展的关注。
• 应用场景的讨论（如ashirviskas和4gotunameagain的评论）展示了Herbie在实际问题（如AI优化和模拟）中的潜在价值。

data.title: Zero-day flaws in authentication, identity, authorization in HashiCorp Vault
data.author: nihsy
data.article_summary: 本文由HashiCorp核心工程师Yarden Porat撰写，详细介绍了他们在HashiCorp Vault中发现的身份验证、身份管理和授权相关的零日漏洞。这些漏洞可能导致未经授权的访问和权限提升。团队通过深入分析Vault的架构和功能，发现了多个安全缺陷，并与HashiCorp合作进行了修复。文章强调了发现和修复这些漏洞的重要性，以保护用户数据和系统安全。同时，也分享了挖掘和分析漏洞的技术细节和方法，为安全研究人员提供了有价值的参考。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：针对Vault Fault漏洞的分析及相关安全问题的讨论

不同观点：
• **shahartal**（Cyata的CEO）: 澄清了漏洞是由人工手动发现的，尽管内容写作过程中有使用文案帮助调整结构和流畅度。表示未来还会有更多相关内容发布。
• **mike_hearn**: 对文章质量表示认可，认为尽管有些许AI写作的痕迹，但内容非常具有信息性。特别指出在安全敏感软件中对字符串处理需谨慎，尤其是将安全标识符视为文本而非固定数字序列时可能带来的漏洞。
• **cipherboy**: 对未提前被告知漏洞表示失望，但感谢社区的贡献。指出OpenBao项目受影响的情况，并对HashiCorp取消开源版本表示不满。
• **neuralkoi**: 认为如果攻击者已获得私钥，问题可能更严重，因此对漏洞的严重性持保留态度。
• **procaryote**: 对文章中不必要的语言解释（如"daka"在希伯来语中的意思）感到困惑，质疑编辑质量。
• **neom**: 详细列出2025年5-6月期间的9个CVE，并对每个漏洞做了简要说明。
• **tptacek**: 认为文章写得不错，但大多数漏洞是情境性的，通常在评估中不会被视为高危。对其中RCE漏洞的发现表示认可，但认为这些漏洞需要管理员权限才能利用。
• **themk**: 对Vault的代码质量表示不满，认为其代码库非常混乱，测试套件不足。
• **AgentMatrixAI**: 提出使用SOPS加API的方式作为Vault的替代方案，认为对小型需求而言足够，不一定需要Vault。
• **technion**: 对"盲用户名枚举"类型的问题表示担忧，认为尽管用户名通常可以被获取，但这类问题仍需重视。
• **unwind**: 认为此讨论与之前的某个帖子内容重复。
• **v5v3**: 质疑某个CVE是否在修复前就被披露，并对信息未公开表示不解。
• **edoceo**: 询问漏洞是否影响Bao项目，建议进行测试。

补充讨论：
- 争议焦点之一是漏洞的严重性和利用难度，部分评论者如tptacek和neuralkoi认为某些漏洞的实际威胁有限。
- 另一个讨论点是HashiCorp取消开源版本的决定，引发cipherboy等对开放性和透明度的关注。
- 对Vault代码质量和测试套件的批评也是一个值得注意的讨论点，themk的观点揭示了对Vault技术实现的深层次担忧。

data.title: 40 Years of the Amiga
data.author: rbanffy
data.article_summary:
1985年7月，Commodore公司发布了Amiga电脑，这款电脑的诞生源于传奇芯片设计师Jay Miner的努力。最初，Amiga项目由Hi-Toro公司启动，旨在开发游戏机，但由于1983年游戏业崩溃，项目转向电脑系统开发。由于资金短缺，Amiga接受了Atari的50万美元投资。然而，1984年Commodore收购Amiga并注资2700万美元。随后，Commodore和Atari因之前的资金纠纷对簿公堂，导致Commodore一度无法公开讨论Amiga。

1985年7月23日，Commodore在纽约林肯中心高调发布Amiga，邀请了名人助阵。尽管早期营销避免直接使用Commodore品牌，但最终Amiga成为了Commodore Amiga。发布后，Amiga迅速引起关注，而其与Atari 520ST的竞争也成为当时话题。尽管发布盛大，作者本人从未实际使用过Amiga，仅通过传闻和评测了解。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Amiga电脑的历史、技术特点、文化影响以及未来发展

• **smartmic**：认为Amiga 2000的独特之处在于其配备了PC桥接板和8088 CPU，尽管功能不全，但能够访问MS-DOS并用GW-BASIC编程，使其不仅可用于游戏，还可用于学校编程学习。

In July 1985, 40 years ago, the Commodore Amiga was officially introduced to the world. This groundbreaking computer caught a lot of people by surprise and it has an equally amazing development story.
As an Atari guy in the 80s, I was somewhat aware of Amiga before 1985 because it would occasionally get mentioned in Atari magazines or by an Atari columnist. I remember seeing a brief note about it in ANALOG Computing and also the Atari column in Creative Computing.
Early History
As many people know, the father of the Amiga is legendary chip designer Jay Miner. He also was the main designer of the Atari 2600 / VCS and the Atari 8-bit computers. Around 1982, he left Atari and went on to work for a company that created pacemaker chips.
Not long after this Miner was contacted by Larry Kaplan, formerly of Atari and a founder of Activision. Kaplan wanted to start his own company (eventually called Hi-Toro) to create a video game system and he thought Miner would be a great person to lead the hardware design.
David Morse was brought in from Tonka to help manage the new company, which soon changed its name to Amiga.
Amiga Joyboard for the Atari 2600
While working on the video game system, Amiga sold products for the Atari 2600 to help fund itself. The early code name for this project was “Lorraine” and “Amiga Lorraine” was the name I had started seeing in rumor columns of various computer magazines. At first this was to be a video game system, but Miner always wanted it to be a computer. When the video game industry crashed in 1983, he got his way and the project pivoted to creating a computer system.
I won’t go into great detail about its creation, but developing a computer system is expensive. With the 1983 crash, Amiga was low on cash and needed additional funds. They ended up securing $500,000 in funding from Atari with an agreement that would allow Atari to use the Amiga technology in video game consoles and computers.

Subscribe
The Shakeup
In early 1984, Commodore CEO Jack Tramiel was ousted from the company (or quit, depending on who you ask) due to a disagreement with its chairman of the board. After a short break, he formed Trammel Technologies
1
to investigate developing a new computer. As luck would have it, right around that time Warner (the owners of Atari) was looking to dump it and the two companies came to an agreement with Jack acquiring Atari from Warner Communications In July 1984. He renamed his nascent Trammel Technologies company to Atari Corp.
About a month later, when it realized it had no viable 16-bit computer in development, Commodore swooped in to buy Amiga for $27 million. Not long after that Atari found details about the Warner Atari $500K loan to Amiga. Lawsuits were filed between the two companies, which  apparently prevented Commodore from publicly discussing the Amiga for some time.
The Announcement
Regardless, Commodore officially announced the Amiga to the world on July 23, 1985. It is an interesting coincidence to me how that date is just a few weeks after Atari started shipping its new 520ST computer.
The Amiga announcement event was quite a spectacle and was held at the Lincoln Center in New York City with celebrities such as Debbie Harry and Andy Warhol helping to promote the new computer.
Initial marketing for the computer focused on the Amiga name and generally avoided direct Commodore branding. In fact, it was often called the “Amiga, from Commodore” back then. I always thought this was a good idea as Amiga is a great computer name, but by 1987 that idea fell out of fashion and it just became the Commodore Amiga.
BTW, some of the early commercials for the Amiga were incredibly strange.
Although I had heard of the Amiga computer via rumors and speculation, I didn’t really know anything about it. To this day, I’ve never used one so I guess you could say I still don’t know much about it!
The first specific details I read about the
Amiga were in the September 1985 issue of Compute! magazine
, which had the Amiga on its cover and included a lengthy feature story about it.
I was somewhat salty about this at the time (and might still be a little today) as this cover story about the Amiga announcement came out a month before Compute!’s review of the actual shipping Atari 520ST. I also didn’t like that they headlined the article with “Amiga: An In-Depth Review”, when it was clearly a product preview at best. Compute! would later redeem itself when it launched the spin-off
Compute!’s Atari ST Disk & Magazine
.
This first Amiga was called the Amiga from Commodore and it is now

data.title: Scientists have recreated the Universe's first molecule
data.author: LAsteNERD
data.article_summary: 科学家成功重现了宇宙中首个分子——氦氢化物离子（HeH⁺），并发现其在早期宇宙中对星体形成起到了关键作用。通过在超低温实验室模拟130亿年前的条件，研究人员发现HeH⁺在冷却早期宇宙中非常有效，使得气体云能够冷却到足以形成第一批恒星。此前理论认为，HeH⁺与氘的反应速率会随温度降低而减慢，但实验表明该反应速率在低温下几乎保持不变，这表明HeH⁺对早期宇宙的冷却和星体形成具有重要影响，可能改写宇宙演化理论。

Scientists just recreated the Universe’s first molecule and solved a 13-billion-year-old puzzle
Researchers have discovered new insights into the reaction pathways of the first molecule in space
Date:
August 3, 2025
Source:
Max-Planck-Institut fur Kernphysik
Summary:
Long before stars lit up the sky, the universe was a hot, dense place where simple chemistry quietly set the stage for everything to come. Scientists have now recreated the first molecule ever to form, helium hydride, and discovered it played a much bigger role in the birth of stars than we thought. Using a special ultra-cold lab setup, they mimicked conditions from over 13 billion years ago and found that this ancient molecule helped cool the universe just enough for stars to ignite. Their findings could rewrite part of the story about how the cosmos evolved from darkness to light.
Share:
Facebook
Twitter
Pinterest
LinkedIN
Email
FULL STORY
Reaction scheme and energetic level of the investigated reaction of the helium hydride ion with deuterium. It is a swift and barrierless reaction, contrary to earlier theories. Background: The planetary nebula NGC 7027, with molecular hydrogen visible in red. Credit: Schematic: MPIK; Background Image: W. B. Latter (SIRTF Science Center/Caltech) and NASA
Immediately after the Big Bang, which occurred around 13.8 billion years ago, the universe was dominated by unimaginably high temperatures and densities. However, after just a few seconds, it had cooled down enough for the first elements to form, primarily hydrogen and helium. These were still completely ionized at this point, as it took almost 380,000 years for the temperature in the universe to drop enough for neutral atoms to form through recombination with free electrons. This paved the way for the first chemical reactions.
The oldest molecule in existence is the helium hydride ion (HeH
+
), formed from a neutral helium atom and an ionized hydrogen nucleus. This marks the beginning of a chain reaction that leads to the formation of molecular hydrogen (H2), which is by far the most common molecule in the universe.
Recombination was followed by the 'dark age' of cosmology: although the universe was now transparent due to the binding of free electrons, there were still no light-emitting objects, such as stars. Several hundred million years passed before the first stars formed.
During this early phase of the universe, however, simple molecules such as HeH⁺ and H2 were essential to the formation of the first stars. In order for the contracting gas cloud of a protostar to collapse to the point where nuclear fusion can begin, heat must be dissipated. This occurs through collisions that excite atoms and molecules, which then emit this energy in the form of photons. Below approximately 10,000 degrees Celsius, however, this process becomes ineffective for the dominant hydrogen atoms. Further cooling can only take place via molecules that can emit additional energy through rotation and vibration. Due to its pronounced dipole moment, the HeH⁺ ion is particularly effective at these low temperatures and has long been considered a potentially important candidate for cooling in the formation of the first stars. Consequently, the concentration of helium hydride ions in the universe may significantly impact the effectiveness of early star formation.
During this period, collisions with free hydrogen atoms were a major degradation pathway for HeH⁺, forming a neutral helium atom and an H2⁺ ion. These subsequently reacted with another H atom to form a neutral H2 molecule and a proton, leading to the formation of molecular hydrogen.
Researchers at the Max-Planck-Institut für Kernphysik (MPIK) in Heidelberg have now successfully recreated this reaction under conditions similar to those in the early universe for the first time. They investigated the reaction of HeH⁺ with deuterium, an isotope of hydrogen containing an additional neutron in the atomic nucleus alongside a proton. When HeH⁺ reacts with deuterium, an HD⁺ ion is formed instead of H2⁺, alongside the neutral helium atom.
The experiment was carried out at the Cryogenic Storage Ring (CSR) at the MPIK in Heidelberg — a globally unique instrument for investigating molecular and atomic reactions under space-like conditions. For this purpose, HeH⁺ ions were stored in the 35-metre-diameter ion storage ring for up to 60 seconds at a few kelvins (-267 °C), and were superimposed with a beam of neutral deuterium atoms. By adjusting the relative speeds of the two particle beams, the scientists were able to study how the collision rate varies with collision energy, which is directly related to temperature.

data.title: Debounce
data.author: aanthonymax
data.article_summary: 本文简要介绍了编程中的去抖动（Debouncing）概念。去抖动通过在特定时间间隔内合并频繁触发的操作来避免过多执行，常用于处理用户输入，如在用户暂停输入后才执行搜索或过滤操作，以防止界面卡顿。去抖动与节流（Throttling）类似，但节流是限制连续操作的频率，而去抖动则是在操作暂停一段时间后才执行。去抖动分为"前缘"（leading edge）和"后缘"（trailing edge），通常在"后缘"执行函数，但具体实现可根据需求在"前缘"、"后缘"或两者上执行。去抖动确保操作至少间隔指定时间（如10毫秒）执行一次。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点： debouncing的概念及其在不同场景下的应用和实现

不同观点：
• **[kazinator]**: 认为将去抖动（debouncing）与减少用户界面中的频繁搜索操作相类比是不恰当的。去抖动是为了解决开关信号的物理问题，而界面操作中，如果有足够的处理能力，每次按键都进行完整搜索是没有问题的，去抖动并不是必须的。开关去抖动与界面去抖动的应用场景不同，处理器速度越快，看到的抖动越多，去抖动问题不会因为更快的微控制器而消失。
  
• **[achou]**: 提到在使用去抖动或节流（throttle）处理异步函数时可能会引发意外行为，尤其是返回的结果可能是之前调用的Promise，而不是当前调用的结果。标准的lodash式实现不支持这种情况，需要特别注意实现是否符合预期。

• **[thomascountz]**: 分享了一个关于使用timeout和AbortController进行fetch去抖动的实现，并提供了示例链接。

• **[ncann]**: 提出在Java中实现去抖动的困难，标准库和常用工具库中缺乏合适的实现，并询问是否有好的推荐。

• **[lma21]**: 提到“合并”（Coalescing）这个术语，并提供了相关的维基百科链接，认为在某些情况下使用这个术语更合适。

• **[Pwntastic]**: 质疑该讨论的价值，认为这个话题并没有特别之处，不值得获得大量投票和关注。

• **[_def]**: 认为去抖动和界面操作的类比是合适的，具体取决于预期的行为，并提供了一个关于去抖动的资源链接。

• **[fnord77]**: 提供了关于开关抖动的维基百科链接。

• **[game_the0ry]**: 提到去抖动已成为前端面试中的热门问题。

• **[G_o_D]**: 通过类比解释了去抖动和节流的概念，并详细描述了它们在用户界面和网络请求处理中的应用场景。

补充讨论：
• 去抖动在不同场景下的实现差异：如[ncann]提到的Java中缺乏合适的去抖动实现，[thomascountz]分享了具体的去抖动实现示例。
• 去抖动与节流的区别和应用：[G_o_D]详细解释了去抖动和节流在处理激进行为和网络请求中的不同作用和实现方式。
• 对去抖动概念类比的争议：[kazinator]和[_def]对去抖动与界面操作的类比有不同看法，前者认为不合适，后者认为合适。

争议的焦点：
• 去抖动与界面操作的类比是否恰当，以及在不同场景下的具体实现和应用。

44787738.article_content:
Debouncing
, in the context of programming, means to discard operations that occur too close together during a specific interval, and consolidate them into a single invocation.
Debouncing is very similar to
throttling
. The key difference is that throttling enforces limits on continuous operations, while debouncing waits for invocations to stop for a specific time to consolidate many noisy invocations into one single invocation.
A typical use case of debouncing is when responding to user input. When the user is typing, no other action should be taken to avoid the UI becoming laggy. When the user pauses typing, we can start processing the input, such as filtering results, giving suggestions, etc. If the function
search
is debounced by 10 milliseconds, it means:
The first call to
search
is known as the
leading edge
.
For every next call to
search
, if it is within 10 milliseconds from the previous call, it is in the same "batch" as the previous call.
After 10 milliseconds have elapsed from the last call to
search
, if no other calls have happened, we have reached the
trailing edge
.
Usually,
search
is executed once on the trailing edge only, although sometimes it might be executed on the leading edge, or even both edges, depending on the specific use case. If executed on both edges, the debouncing implementation usually also ensures that the next leading edge invocation doesn't fire at least 10 milliseconds after the previous trailing edge.

44787738.article_summary: 本文简要介绍了编程中的去抖动（Debouncing）概念。去抖动通过在特定时间间隔内合并频繁触发的操作来避免过多执行，常用于处理用户输入，如在用户暂停输入后才执行搜索或过滤操作，以防止界面卡顿。去抖动与节流（Throttling）类似，但节流是限制连续操作的频率，而去抖动则是在操作暂停一段时间后才执行。去抖动分为"前缘"（leading edge）和"后缘"（trailing edge），通常在"后缘"执行函数，但具体实现可根据需求在"前缘"、"后缘"或两者上执行。去抖动确保操作至少间隔指定时间（如10毫秒）执行一次。
44787738.comments_summary:
主要讨论点： debouncing的概念及其在不同场景下的应用和实现

不同观点：
• **[kazinator]**: 认为将去抖动（debouncing）与减少用户界面中的频繁搜索操作相类比是不恰当的。去抖动是为了解决开关信号的物理问题，而界面操作中，如果有足够的处理能力，每次按键都进行完整搜索是没有问题的，去抖动并不是必须的。开关去抖动与界面去抖动的应用场景不同，处理器速度越快，看到的抖动越多，去抖动问题不会因为更快的微控制器而消失。
  
• **[achou]**: 提到在使用去抖动或节流（throttle）处理异步函数时可能会引发意外行为，尤其是返回的结果可能是之前调用的Promise，而不是当前调用的结果。标准的lodash式实现不支持这种情况，需要特别注意实现是否符合预期。

• **[thomascountz]**: 分享了一个关于使用timeout和AbortController进行fetch去抖动的实现，并提供了示例链接。

• **[ncann]**: 提出在Java中实现去抖动的困难，标准库和常用工具库中缺乏合适的实现，并询问是否有好的推荐。

• **[lma21]**: 提到“合并”（Coalescing）这个术语，并提供了相关的维基百科链接，认为在某些情况下使用这个术语更合适。

• **[Pwntastic]**: 质疑该讨论的价值，认为这个话题并没有特别之处，不值得获得大量投票和关注。

• **[_def]**: 认为去抖动和界面操作的类比是合适的，具体取决于预期的行为，并提供了一个关于去抖动的资源链接。

• **[fnord77]**: 提供了关于开关抖动的维基百科链接。

• **[game_the0ry]**: 提到去抖动已成为前端面试中的热门问题。

• **[G_o_D]**: 通过类比解释了去抖动和节流的概念，并详细描述了它们在用户界面和网络请求处理中的应用场景。

补充讨论：
• 去抖动在不同场景下的实现差异：如[ncann]提到的Java中缺乏合适的去抖动实现，[thomascountz]分享了具体的去抖动实现示例。
• 去抖动与节流的区别和应用：[G_o_D]详细解释了去抖动和节流在处理激进行为和网络请求中的不同作用和实现方式。
• 对去抖动概念类比的争议：[kazinator]和[_def]对去抖动与界面操作的类比有不同看法，前者认为不合适，后者认为合适。

争议的焦点：
• 去抖动与界面操作的类比是否恰当，以及在不同场景下的具体实现和应用。

data.article_summary: GitHub accidentally revealed details about OpenAI's upcoming GPT-5 models through a now-deleted blog post. The GPT-5 models, set to launch soon, will feature "enhanced agentic capabilities" and be able to handle complex coding tasks with minimal prompting. The models will be available in four variants: gpt-5, gpt-5-mini, gpt-5-nano, and gpt-5-chat, each designed for different purposes ranging from logic and multi-step tasks to lightweight and low-latency applications. OpenAI is also planning a live stream event for the official launch. Additionally, the company recently released two GPT open-weight models, one of which can run on a local PC.

GitHub has accidentally announced OpenAI’s new range of GPT-5 models. A now-deleted GitHub blog post reveals that GPT-5, which will be available in four different versions, offers “major improvements in reasoning, code quality, and user experience.”
Reddit
posters noticed a new GitHub blog post announcing that GPT-5 is generally available in GitHub models, before the blog post was quickly removed. An
archived version
reveals that GPT-5 will have “enhanced agentic capabilities” and can handle “complex coding tasks with minimal prompting.”
GitHub also compared GPT-5 to Llama 4 Scout and Cohere v2.
Image: GitHub
GPT-5 will have four model variants, according to GitHub:
gpt-5
: Designed for logic and multi-step tasks.
gpt-5-mini
: A lightweight version for cost-sensitive applications.
gpt-5-nano
: Optimized for speed and ideal for applications requiring low latency.
gpt-5-chat
: Designed for advanced, natural, multimodal, and context-aware conversations for enterprise applications.
I revealed last month that OpenAI was
preparing to launch GPT-5 in early August
, complete with mini and nano versions that will also be available through its API. Earlier this week multiple OpenAI employees
started teasing
that it would be a big week, and OpenAI CEO Sam Altman even teased GPT-5 over the weekend.
OpenAI has all but confirmed it’s launching GPT-5 later today,
with the announcement
of a “LIVE5TREAM” for 10AM PT / 1PM ET. OpenAI’s GPT-5 launch comes in the same week the company also delivered two
GPT-OSS open-weight models
, with one small enough to run locally on a PC.

data.title: Show HN: Kitten TTS – 25MB CPU-Only, Open-Source TTS Model
data.author: divamgupta
data.article_summary: KittenTTS 是一个开源的文本到语音（TTS）模型，模型大小不到25MB，具有1500万参数，专为轻量级部署和高质量语音合成设计。它具备超轻量、CPU优化、高音质和快速推理等特点，适合在各种设备上运行而无需GPU。用户可以通过简单的Python代码调用KittenTTS生成语音，并有多种优质声音可选。当前处于开发者预览阶段，未来计划发布完整模型、移动SDK和网页版本。项目遵循Apache-2.0许可证，已在GitHub获得3.7k星标。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：KittenTTS模型的性能、质量、应用场景及技术挑战

不同观点：
• 支持与期待观点：
  - [nine_k] 认为KittenTTS代表了未来的方向，支持离线运行的小型ML模型可以在普遍且廉价的硬件上运行，易于与其他设备和应用程序集成。
  - [toisanji] 同样表示支持，希望看到更多能在CPU上运行的优秀模型。
  - [vahid4m] 表示期待将KittenTTS集成到现有项目中，认为像KittenTTS这样的基础工具为一次性支付或免费工具提供了可能性。

• 性能与技术讨论：
  - [peanut_merchant] 提供了详细的性能基准测试结果，显示模型在不同文本长度下的音频生成速度和初始延迟。
  - [MutedEstate45] 强调KittenTTS的Apache-2.0许可证与其小体积的组合，使其能够在低端硬件上运行，无需担心GPU和云调用。
  - [blopker] 提供了一个Web版本的链接，认为音频质量对于模型大小来说是可以接受的。
  - [antisol] 指出在不同机器上由于Python版本问题导致安装困难。
  - [klipklop] 提到尽管模型本身小，但安装所需的库和依赖项使得总体大小远超25MB。

• 质量与应用对比：
  - [keyle] 关注延迟问题，并询问是否有离线语音转文本的模型，期待能与AI进行自然对话。
  - [sandreas] 认为KittenTTS质量不足以替代更大的模型，提到了fish-speech和F5-TTS等其他开源模型，认为它们在质量上更具优势。
  - [wkat4242] 对KittenTTS的音质不满意，认为不如kokoro和XTTS，但赞赏Whisper在语音转文本方面的表现。
  - [dr_kiszonka] 提到微软和谷歌的TTS模型有时会犯简单的错误，如将"i.e."读作"for example"，并对此表示好奇。

• 语言支持与扩展性：
  - [spapas82] 询问KittenTTS是否支持其他语言，或者能否通过训练支持其他语言。

补充讨论：
• 技术挑战与改进空间：
  - 安装过程中的兼容性问题和所需依赖项的大小问题被多次提到，表明在实际应用中仍存在技术障碍。
  - 对于音质和延迟的改进期望，特别是在与其他TTS模型的对比中，KittenTTS仍有提升空间。
  
• 许可证与部署优势：
  - KittenTTS的Apache-2.0许可证被视为一个重要优势，使得其在嵌入式设备和商业应用中具有潜力。

争议焦点：
• KittenTTS的音质和延迟是否能满足广泛应用的需求，以及与其他高质量TTS模型的对比。

  - [klipklop] 提到尽管模型本身小，但安装所需的库和依赖项使得总体大小远超25MB。

• 质量与应用对比：
  - [keyle] 关注延迟问题，并询问是否有离线语音转文本的模型，期待能与AI进行自然对话。
  - [sandreas] 认为KittenTTS质量不足以替代更大的模型，提到了fish-speech和F5-TTS等其他开源模型，认为它们在质量上更具优势。
  - [wkat4242] 对KittenTTS的音质不满意，认为不如kokoro和XTTS，但赞赏Whisper在语音转文本方面的表现。
  - [dr_kiszonka] 提到微软和谷歌的TTS模型有时会犯简单的错误，如将"i.e."读作"for example"，并对此表示好奇。

• 语言支持与扩展性：
  - [spapas82] 询问KittenTTS是否支持其他语言，或者能否通过训练支持其他语言。

补充讨论：
• 技术挑战与改进空间：
  - 安装过程中的兼容性问题和所需依赖项的大小问题被多次提到，表明在实际应用中仍存在技术障碍。
  - 对于音质和延迟的改进期望，特别是在与其他TTS模型的对比中，KittenTTS仍有提升空间。
  
• 许可证与部署优势：
  - KittenTTS的Apache-2.0许可证被视为一个重要优势，使得其在嵌入式设备和商业应用中具有潜力。

争议焦点：
• KittenTTS的音质和延迟是否能满足广泛应用的需求，以及与其他高质量TTS模型的对比。

44820619.article_content:
Actual LLM agents are coming
Mar 13, 2025
Agents are everywhere these days. And yet, the most consequential research development in agentic LLM research is almost unnoticed.
In January 2025, OpenAI released
DeepResearch
, a specialized variant of O3 for web and document search. Thanks to "reinforcement learning training on these browsing tasks", Deep Research has gained the capacity to plan for a search strategy, cross-reference sources and
niche piece of knowledge
on queries based on intermediary feedback. Claude Sonnet 3.7 seems to apply successfully the same recipe for code. The model alone outperform existing orchestrations of past models on complex sequences of programming tasks.
In short, as William Brown
puts
it, "LLM agents can work for long multi-step tasks".
This advancement raises the question of what LLM agents really are. In December, Anthropic
unveiled
a new definition: "systems where LLMs dynamically direct their own processes and tool usage, maintaining control over how they accomplish tasks."
In contrast, all the more commons form of agentic system are contrasted as
our
, "where LLMs and tools are orchestrated through predefined code paths". The recently hyped Manus AI fits exactly this definition. All our tests
show
the same fundamental limitations of workflow systems that were already apparent in the time of AutoGPT, and are
especially striking for search
:
* They can't plan and frequently get stuck in the middle of nowhere.
* They can't memorize and struggle to maintain a task for more than 5-10 minutes.
* They can't act effectively in the long run. Sequence of actions routinely fail due to a compounded error effect.
This post takes as a starting point an new strong definition of LLM agents. It does its best at summarizing what we know so far, based on a mix of limited information from big labs, emerging reproduction in the open research ecosystem and some personal speculation.
The bitter lesson of simple LLM agents
The concept of agents almost entirely clashes with base language models.
In classic agentic research, agents inhabits constrained environments. You're in a maze, you can move in this direction, but not this one. And you cannot fly, nor get under the ground, nor disappear in thin air. You're constrained by physics and, optionally, by the rules of the game. Any actual agents placed in this situation can still enjoy some degree of freedom, as there is more than one way to solve a game. Yet every move have to be conceived under the assumption of winning, getting your final reward. Effective agents gradually memorize past moves and elaborate patterns and heuristics.
This process is called "
search
". It's a very fitting metaphor: the exploratory move of an agent in a maze is a total analog to the clicking patterns of a web user on a search engines. There is a decades-long literature about search: suffice to notice that
Q-star
, the algorithm once rumored to be behind the new O generation of OpenAI model (it's unclearâ¦), is an offshot of
A-Star
, a search algorithm from 1968. One of the best recent example of this process is the
Pokemon training experiment
done by Pufferlib: we see the agents literally searching for the optimal paths, failing, going back and forth.
Base language models work almost exactly in reverse:
* Agents are memorizing their environment. Base models don't and can only react to the information available inside their context window.
* Agents are constrained by bounded rationality. Base models are generating any probable text. While that may result in actually consistent reasoning there is no hard guarantee and models can deviate at any time under pure aesthetic moves.
* Agents can devise long term strategies. If they well conceived they can plan ahead moves in advance or backtrack. Language models are able to perform single-reasoning task but will quickly [saturate for multi-hop reasoning](https://stochasm.blog/posts/contextualization-machines/). Overall they are bounded by text rules, not physics/game rules.
A simple way of reconciling LLM and agentification would be to simply predefine their output through prepared prompts and rules. This is the approach retained by most agentic LLM systems and bound to hit on theâ¦
Bitter lesson
from Richard Sutton. The Bitter Lesson is sometimes mistaken as some kind of guidebook to pretraining language models. It is really primarily about agents and about the temptation of incorporating and harcoding knowledge into the models. If you're seeing a wall, avoid it, move in the other direction. If you're seeing too many walls, backtrack. This is nice in the short term, you'll see immediate improvement and you won't have to run an algorithm forever to see them. In the long run, though, you are bound to always find suboptimal solution or get stuck into unexpected setting:

by
Lucian Constantin
CSO Senior Writer
Researchers uncover RCE attack chains in popular enterprise credential vaults
News Analysis
Aug 6, 2025
9 mins
Identity and Access Management
Open Source
Remote Access Security
Open-source credential management systems HashiCorp Vault and CyberArk Conjur had flaws enabled remote code execution among other attacks.
Credit:
NicoElNino/Shutterstock
Researchers have found 14 logic flaws in various components of HashiCorp Vault and CyberArk Conjur, two open-source credential management systems, allowing attacks that could bypass authentication checks, access secrets, impersonate identities and execute arbitrary code.
In enterprise environments, non-human identities, such as those used by applications and machines, are estimated to outnumber human identities 150 to 1. This makes credential management systems, which often hold what can be considered the “keys to the kingdom,” a critical component of IT infrastructure.
Recognizing this, researchers from cybersecurity firm Cyata analyzed two widely used open-source secrets management solutions: HashiCorp Vault and CyberArk Conjur. Their findings, which include 14 vulnerabilities that enable remote code execution (RCE) attack chains in both products, were presented today at the Black Hat USA security conference in Las Vegas.
“Secrets vaults are the backbone of digital infrastructure,” the researchers wrote in
their report
. “They store the credentials, tokens, and certificates that govern access to systems, services, APIs, and data. They’re not just part of the trust model — they are the trust model. In other words, if your vault is compromised, your infrastructure is already lost.”
HashiCorp Vault and CyberArk Conjur do more than just store secrets. They allow organizations to define policies for accessing and using those secrets, offering role-based access controls, automated secrets rotation, auditing, and more. Designed for integration with DevOps tools, these systems are often part of CI/CD pipelines.
The attack chains discovered by Cyata, responsibly disclosed to HashiCorp and CyberArk and now patched, stemmed from subtle logic flaws in authentication, validation, and policy enforcement mechanisms. The flaws enabled lockout bypasses, policy check evasion and account impersonation.
Missing validation checks enable Conjur compromise
Cyata’s attack chain against CyberArk Conjur began with a simple error in the code used to validate AWS IAM identities. Conjur supports authentication for AWS instances via AWS’s Security Token Service (STS), allowing workflows to authenticate without hardcoded credentials.
To authenticate, an AWS instance generates a signed header, which Conjur forwards to AWS STS. STS validates the signature and returns the instance’s identity. However, STS servers are region-specific. For example, instances in us-east-1 must use sts.us-east-1.amazonaws.com and Conjur determines the correct STS region based on the instance’s hostname included in the signed header.
The issue is that the hostname in the header can be controlled by the attacker. And while this wouldn’t be a problem because a fake signature would normally fail validation by a legitimate STS instance, Conjur’s code failed to sanitize special characters like ‘?’ in the hostname.
This allowed researchers to craft a request with a hostname such as sts.cyata.ai?, which the Conjur code transformed into sts.cyata.ai?.amazonaws.com, appending the correct domain. However, in practice, the portion after the added question mark gets ignored in URLs so the requests get sent to sts.cyata.ai, a rogue STS server under the researchers’ control, passing validation.
“This was the first step in the chain, where a completely unauthenticated attacker could now enter the system, appearing to be a legitimate AWS identity,” the researchers explained.
From identity forgery to full RCE
An AWS instance identity typically corresponds to a hostname. But the researchers explored how this could be abused within Conjur’s resource model, which uses three parameters: Account (Conjur account name), Kind (resource type — host, user, variable, policy, etc.), and Identifier (unique resource name). These parameters are also used in API queries.
They discovered that Conjur’s authentication logic didn’t validate the “kind” part of an identity. This meant they could use their spoofed AWS identity to authenticate as a user or policy in the system instead of a host, significantly expanding the attack surface.
“This step changed the game,” they said. “It bridged the gap between unauthenticated access and a meaningful attack surface in Conjur. By combining a forged STS response, a policy identity instead of a host, and flaws in the Host Factory flow, we gained the ability to mint new hosts with names and ownership entirely under our control.”

data.title: Atlassian's Trello redesign may be 'worst in tech history' say frustrated users
data.author: mindracer
data.article_summary: Atlassian's recent redesign of its Trello project management tool has sparked widespread user backlash. Customers have compared the update to notorious software failures like Microsoft's Windows 8, citing disappearing features and a confusing new interface. Many users have vented their frustration on the Trello community forum and Reddit, demanding a return to the old design. Some speculate that Atlassian is attempting to push professional users towards its more expensive Jira tool. Despite the company's claim that over 20% of users have opted into the new design's beta program, many feel the changes hinder productivity and are calling for reversals.

Skype redesign
,
Accenture's Hertz site debacle

GitHub's bungled code search renovation

This update is possibly the worst in tech history
The Trello revision
debuted on May 22, 2025
. It changed how interface elements are arranged on the page, altering the layout, fonts, and button functions. Some capabilities, like the ability to add comments to cards, disappeared.
On the company's
Trello community forum
, a thread started in June has accumulated almost 200 posts, largely from people complaining about the design change.
Here's a dissatisfaction sampler:
"

."

," by user mnmacguy, offers a blistering assessment of the changes.
"People are comparing this to the worst software updates in history," the post says. "One user said, 'This is the worst UI update I’ve ever seen, including Windows 8.' If you’re being measured against Windows 8, that should say something."

wrote
, "This update is arguably one of the worst in the past five years, and possibly in tech history, which is quite disappointing."

for Trello.

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI伦理与安全的实际应用、治理结构、以及伦理标准的争议

不同观点：
• **nisten**：认为AI伦理和安全组织的问题在于，他们的工作重点不是解决实际问题，如提高食品和住房的可负担性，而是放在缺乏“治理结构”上。他们往往不从事实际的技术工作，也不提出具体的解决方案，只是空谈伦理和安全问题。

• **Isamu**：指出AI伦理讨论中存在回避具体风险（如对人类的伤害）的倾向，而不是提供合理的论证来说明为什么某些概念（如阿西莫夫定律）过时。

• **i_dont_know_**：认为“AI伦理”被重新定义为关注虚构问题而不是现实世界的问题，并对此表示担忧。

• **lr4444lr**：将AI伦理比作核伦理，认为如果没有强有力的国际协议和后果，打破伦理的诱惑是巨大的。

• **mitthrowaway2**：认为伦理是一个广泛的领域，而安全只是其中的一个子集，许多伦理问题并不涉及安全问题。

• **mystraline**：质疑“伦理”的具体定义和公理，担心伦理被用作掩盖偏见和逃避质疑的工具。

• **parpfish**：更关注当前机器学习模型带来的伦理问题，如深度伪造和算法偏见，而不是未来可能出现的超级智能问题。

• **blibble**：认为当前一些科技领袖（如扎克伯格、马斯克等）已经是“不受约束的实体”，AI只会增加他们施加影响的范围和能力。

• **kyoob**：指出讨论从实际的治理和责任问题突然转向科幻场景（如AI接管世界），缺乏一贯性。

• **Workaccount2**：猜测可能越少的 safeguards 和 thought policing，模型的能力和泛化能力越强，从而使那些低 safeguards 的模型最强大。

• **saurik**：批评当前AI伦理工作更多关注公关问题，而不是实际的技术风险，如模型失控或接管世界，并认为模型的首要目标应该是完全服从用户指令。

• **akakajzbzbbx**：认为人类自身无法就什么是伦理/安全达成一致，因此对将伦理应用到AI上表示怀疑。

• **nathias**：质疑那些自称“伦理学家”的人的专业资质，认为许多所谓的伦理领域实际上只是公关部门。

• **p3rls**：以幽默的方式指出AI伦理讨论中的实际技术问题，如他们的机器人导致服务器过载。

补充讨论：
• **讨论之间的关系**：评论者之间存在对AI伦理实际应用与理论讨论的争议，部分评论者（如nisten和saurik）批评伦理讨论缺乏技术深度和实际解决方案，而其他人（如Isamu和parpfish）则关注具体风险和当前问题。
• **争议的焦点**：AI伦理的定义和实际应用、治理结构的重要性、以及伦理讨论中的技术与非技术问题之间的平衡。

data.title: Show HN: Stasher – Burn-after-read secrets from the CLI, no server, no trust
data.author: stasher-dev
data.article_summary: Stasher CLI是一款开源的命令行工具，用于安全、临时地分享秘密信息。它采用零知识加密（AES-256-GCM）在本地加密，并通过"阅后即焚"机制确保秘密只能被读取一次。Stasher没有后端服务器，不需注册账户，所有操作在终端完成，且10分钟后自动失效。所有代码和依赖都是公开且可验证的，确保透明性和安全性。用户可以通过`npx enstash`创建秘密并获取一个`uuid:key`，通过`npx destash`读取并永久删除该秘密。该工具适用于快速、安全地分享一次性密码、文件等敏感信息。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于密码分享工具的安全性、实现方式及信任问题

不同观点：
• [支持使用专用工具的观点]  
   有用户（如[indigodaddy]）推荐使用现有的密码分享工具如Password Pusher，认为其部署简单且功能合理，默认设置安全，是适合用于密码分享的工具。

• [质疑工具安全性的观点]  
   多位用户（如[Disposal8433]、[cmeacham98]、[pxc]）对该密码分享工具的安全性提出质疑。他们指出，工具的代码疑似由AI生成，项目作者匿名，且项目缺乏社区支持。这些因素使得用户不愿意信任该工具，尤其在安全敏感的场景下。

• [建议使用其他替代方案的观点]  
   有用户（如[i_proteus]、[precompute]）建议使用GPG等成熟的加密工具，或者对于非技术用户，推荐使用Signal、消失消息等更简便的方案。这些替代方案被认为更可靠且易于理解。

• [关于工具设计和流程的争议]  
   用户[coldstartops]质疑工具的流程设计，认为其将简单的两步操作复杂化，并引入服务器作为中间人，增加了风险。相比之下，[scosman]认为直接发送加密文本（如uuid:cipertext）也能达到相同的安全效果，且避免服务器接触敏感数据。

补充讨论：
• [服务器作用的疑问]  
   用户[h43z]询问服务器是否仅用于确保密码只被读取一次，表明对工具具体功能存在疑问。

• [“burn-after-read”概念的解释]  
   用户[oats]询问“burn-after-read”的含义，其他用户解释为密码在第一次读取后即不可再次获取。

• [命令行历史记录的安全问题]  
   用户[jijji]提到命令行操作可能被记录到.bash_history中，建议在执行敏感操作时调整历史记录设置以增强安全性。

• [盲目信任的争议]  
   用户[Thatdudeyouknow]简单表示“Trust me bro!”，这种盲目信任的态度与其他用户对安全性严格审查的态度形成对比，反映出在安全问题上不应轻率。

争议的焦点：工具的安全性、代码透明度、服务器的作用以及是否需要信任工具作者。

🛡️ Stasher CLI
Share secrets from your terminal. One-time only. No accounts. No backend. No BS.
🤔 Why?
I just wanted to share a password.
Not spin up a server. Not sign up for a "secure" web app.
Not trust a Slack thread. Just. Send. A. Secret.
So I built Stasher — a burn-after-read, command-line tool for secure, ephemeral secret sharing.
Built for people who are busy, paranoid, or both.
🔍 "How Can I Trust You?"
That's what someone asked me — and they were right to.
Even if I say:
"It's encrypted"
"The key never touches the server"
"No logs, no tracking, no metadata"...
How do you know I'm not lying?
🧠 I realized: the more secrecy your secrets require, the more transparency my system must offer.
So I built Stasher to prove itself.
🔐 Everything Is Verifiable
Every Stasher release:
✅ Is cryptographically signed with Cosign
✅ Includes a SLSA v1 provenance attestation
✅ Publishes a signed SBOM with all dependencies + licenses
✅ Is logged in the Rekor transparency log
✅ Comes with full verification instructions
📖 Every Line of Code Is Public
Everything that runs Stasher is open and verifiable:
🔧
CLI
🛰️
API
🖥️
App
⚙️
CI/CD
🌐
Website
🛡️ The only thing we don't expose? Your secret. Everything else is yours to inspect.
💡 Why You Might Actually Care
🔐
Zero-knowledge encryption
– AES-256-GCM, done locally
💣
Burn-after-read
– one use, then it's gone forever
🧰
CLI-first
– pipe it, script it, automate it
⚡
No setup
– just run it with
npx
⌛
10-minute expiry
– with proactive + reactive cleanup
📜
Full supply chain transparency
– signed, attested, and public
🚀 Try It Now
npx enstash
"
the launch code is 🍌-42
"
#
→ Outputs: uuid:key
npx destash
"
uuid:key
"
#
→ Reveals the secret and deletes it forever
🔐 Trust, But Actually Verify
#
Verify latest release
VERSION=
$(
npm view stasher-cli version
)
npm pack stasher-cli@
$VERSION
cosign verify-blob \
--certificate-identity-regexp=
"
https://github.com/stasher-dev/stasher-cli/.*
"
\
--certificate-oidc-issuer=https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com \
--signature=
"
stasher-cli-
$VERSION
.tgz.sig
"
\
"
stasher-cli-
$VERSION
.tgz
"
📚 More:
📖 Verification Overview
🔐 Cosign Signatures
🧾 SLSA Attestation
📋 SBOM Verification
📜 Rekor Transparency
🛠 Usage
Enstash (Create a Secret)
#
From a string
enstash
"
don't forget to feed the AI
"
#
From a file
cat .env
|
enstash
#
From stdin with npx
echo
"
my passphrase is secret123
"
|
npx enstash
Destash (Read + Burn)
destash
"
uuid:base64key
"
npx destash
"
uuid:base64key
"
Unstash (Manual Delete)
unstash
"
uuid
"
unstash
"
uuid:base64key
"
🧪 Examples
#
Share Wi-Fi password with a guest
npx enstash
"
yesits1234dontjudge
"
#
Send a one-time OTP via Slack
npx enstash
"
OTP: 842991
"
#
Share a deployment key, then delete it
echo
"
DEPLOY_KEY=super-secret
"
|
npx enstash
npx unstash
"
uuid
"
#
Send a secret via pigeon 🐦
npx enstash
"
vault code: 1234#
"
#
(Remind them: 10-minute expiry)
🔍 How It Works
🔐
Client-Side Encryption
Stasher encrypts with
AES-256-GCM
before sending anything
It uploads: ciphertext, IV, and tag —
never the key
You get a
uuid:base64key
token to share
⏱
Hybrid Expiry System
Reactive expiry
: validated on every access
Proactive cleanup
: background Durable Object alarms
Atomic
: each stash is guarded by its own isolated gatekeeper (one DO per UUID)
💥
Burn-After-Read
Once
destash
is called, the secret is revealed and the stash is burned
No replays, no race conditions —
guaranteed

npm install -g stasher-cli
…but honestly?
npx
is faster and cleaner.

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：[学校监控和政府干预的合理性及其对学生的影响]

不同观点：
• **反对过度监控和干预**  
  - [paradox460]和[malwrar]认为监控会让学生习惯于被监视，进而接受未来的大规模监控社会，这种“懒惰的压迫”对社会有害。  
  - [kayodelycaon]和[IshKebab]批评对13岁女孩的过度反应（如脱衣搜查和监禁），认为这种处理方式可能加剧问题而非解决。  
  - [Atreiden]指出，孩子因缺乏语境而说蠢话是正常的，自动联系执法部门是“反乌托邦”行为。  

• **支持监控但反对政府滥用**  
  - [tyleo]区分学校监控自有平台（可以接受）和政府监控私人通讯（不可接受），认为文章混淆了二者。  
  - [zahlman]指出学校因法律强制（如田纳西州零容忍政策）不得不采取极端措施，责任应归咎于政府而非企业。  

• **质疑监控的实际效果**  
  - [clwncr]质疑学校声称监控“阻止暴力”的说法，认为缺乏数据支持，且虚假 positives 的代价过高（如逮捕、心理评估）。  
  - [giantg2]批评执行者的懒惰，认为自动化系统的判断被盲目采信，导致过度反应。  

• **其他争议点**  
  - [SeanDav]提到法院的后续处理（如居家监禁）可能验证了事件的严重性，但缺乏家长通知仍不合理。  
  - [evaXhill]讽刺通过监控解决校园枪击的荒诞性，建议限制枪支获取而非侵犯隐私。  

补充讨论：  
- 争议焦点：监控的边界（如学校自有平台 vs. 私人通讯）、政府与学校的责任划分、虚假 positives 的社会代价。  
- 隐含讨论：如何平衡安全与自由，以及监控是否真正有效（如[ludicrousdispla]的讽刺暗示系统可能过度敏感）。

data.title: Leonardo Chiariglione: “I closed MPEG on 2 June 2020”
data.author: eggspurt
data.article_summary: Leonardo Chiariglione，一位拥有跨文化技术背景和基督教天主教教育背景的工程师，致力于开发可互操作的数字媒体技术。1987年，他创立了**MPEG（动态图像专家组）**，该组织在随后几年制定了多项重要标准，如MPEG-1、MPEG-2和MPEG-4，推动了数字媒体时代的到来。然而，由于一些不明势力的干预，MPEG逐渐失去活力，技术发展停滞，知识产权授权模式过时，导致行业和消费者无法受益于新技术。2020年6月，Chiariglione离开MPEG，随后于2020年7月提出成立**MPAI（人工智能编码的动态图像、音频和数据）**，旨在开发基于强大技术的新标准，打破僵局。MPAI已经制定了五项标准，并有多个项目正在进行中，涵盖AI应用、音频增强、多模态对话等领域。Chiariglione通过其著作和博客记录了MPEG的兴衰及MPAI的成长。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：MPEG标准的兴衰、专利对技术发展的阻碍、以及新组织和技术的潜力

不同观点：
• **ZeroGravitas的观点**：认为MPEG引擎在技术和商业上已经失去动力，被大公司利用以谋取专利利益，阻碍了技术发展。这些公司通过专利设置障碍，限制了新技术的市场采用，导致行业受限，消费者无法受益。举例提到2002年Steve Jobs拒绝发布新版Quicktime，直到AAC许可问题得到解决。

• **wheybags的观点**：认为MPEG长期以来通过h264、h265和mp3等专利阻碍了行业发展。如果这些专利的铁腕控制被打破，可能会带来更多创新机会。

• **marcodiego的观点**：批评MPEG负责人过去的作为，认为其参与了专利垄断，并在失去权力后才抱怨。这种虚伪行为被视为“最精致的伪善”。

• **dostick的观点**：质疑所谓“ obscure forces”到底是什么，并提出疑问：作为一个开放标准的非营利组织，为何会受到阻碍？推测可能是因为技术上更优越的封闭标准出现，导致非营利项目难以竞争。提到USB联盟的成功例子，建议压缩标准可以类似方式发展。

• **kouru225的观点**：关注MPEG创始人新成立的组织MPAI，希望了解更多关于该组织的评价和技术细节。

• **mananaysiempre的观点**：提供背景信息，指出MPEG关闭时其所有页面和资料被删除并重定向至AI内容，暗示可能存在利益冲突。

• **karel-3d的观点**：对AI与视频编解码器的关系感到困惑，表明对两者的技术理解不深。

• **selvan的观点**：认为基于深度学习的专利免费视频编解码技术可能在几年内出现，提到微软开发的DCVC-RT编解码器，并讨论了AI在音视频编解码器开发中的潜力。

• **_bent的观点**：质疑MPAI社区提出的标准，认为某些标准没有必要，因为不同游戏服务器之间不需要互操作性。

• **zazazx的观点**：简短评论，强调行业对MPEG的利用和操纵。

• **gcr的观点**：欢迎MPEG组的结束，认为开放编解码器的兴起是积极的进展。虽然承认MPEG早期的工作有价值，但认为到2005年左右应转向更开放的互操作性模型。

• **scotty79的观点**：建议对知识产权持有者征收“财产税”以改善系统健康，批评版权制度阻碍创新，认为AI行业可能会摧毁这一制度。

补充讨论：
• **专利与技术发展**：多个评论提到了专利制度对技术发展的阻碍，尤其是MPEG相关的专利许可模型对行业和消费者的负面影响。
• **AI与编解码器的结合**：讨论了AI技术在未来编解码器开发中的潜在应用和优势，以及可能带来的创新。
• **非营利组织与商业标准的竞争**：探讨了非营利标准组织如何在面对商业技术竞争时保持竞争力，以及可能的组织模式借鉴。

争议焦点：
• **MPEG的功过**：一方认为MPEG早期贡献大，但后期阻碍了技术发展；另一方则认为其整体上是一个被大公司操控的专利垄断工具。
• **专利制度的存废**：讨论中涉及是否应通过征税或彻底打破专利制度来促进技术进步。

44822637.article_content:
Leonardo - one time video coding researcher, standardisation veteran and entrepreneur
I received a high-school education that gave me a Western classic imprint (Salesian Lyceum Valsalice, Maturità), an engineer’s  technical education (Polytechnic of Turin, MSc in Electronic Engineering) and a cross-cultural/technical experience (University of Tokyo, PhD in Electrical Communications).
My Christian Catholic education made and still makes me think that everybody should have a mission that extends beyond their personal interests.
In my early professional years, when digital media technologies were still maturing, I saw my mission in
the development of interoperable digital media technologies for
society
to enjoy
and
industry
to exploit
.
I needed an organisation that would
create digital media standards for
consumers
to seamlessly communicate and
industry
operate in a global market of interoperable products, services and applications
.
I conceived
t
hat organisation
in 1987, established it in 1988
I, and called
Moving Picture Experts Group
(MPEG). In four years,
MPEG had
ushered in the
digital media age
with
MPEG-1,
a standard for interactive media
used in Video CD, digital audio broadcasting (MP2), and personal music (MP3). Starting from the mid ’90s, MPEG-2, the result of the second MPEG project, became the common infrastructure that underpinned distribution of digital television via cable, satellite, terrestrial networks and package media (DVD). MPEG-4, the third standard first released in 1988, opened the way to digital media distribution over the internet. Several families of standards followed: MPEG-7, MPEG-21,
MPEG-A, MPEG-H, MPEG-I and more.
I chaired the group
fostering its productivity with the development of over 200 standards, membership with a 20-fold growth in attendance
from the initial 29 experts attending the first meeting, and scope extending from media to genomics, the “born digital” data of the world..
I closed MPEG on 2 June 2020 when I left because
obscure forces
had hijacked it.
Even before it has ceased to exists, the MPEG engine had run out of steam – technology- and business wise. The same obscure forces that have hijacked MPEG had kept it hostage to their interests impeding its technical development and keeping it locked to outmoded Intellectual Property licensing models delaying market adoption of MPEG standards. Industry has been strangled
and consumers have been deprived of the benefits of new technologies. From
facilitators
of new opportunities and experiences, MPEG s
tandards have morphed from
into
roadblocks.
On the 19th of July 2020 I proposed and, on 30 September 2020, a group of 33 companies established the
Moving Picture, Audio and Data Coding by Artificial Intelligence
(MPAI). Industry and consumers have now an organisation developing standards based on powerful technologies, overcoming stagnation and licensing stalemates. Five standards covering
execution of AI applications
,
audio enhancement
,
multimodal conversation
,
company performance prediction
, and
ecosystem governance
have been developed and adopted. More standards are in the pipeline:
AI-based End-to-End Video Coding
,
AI-Enhanced Video Coding
,
AI Health
,
Avatar Representation and Animation
,
Connected Autonomous Vehicles
,
Metaverse Model
,
Server-based Predictive Multiplayer Gaming
, and
XR Venues
.
The book
Even the stars die
tell the MPEG story from birth to death and the MPAI story from birth to growth to death. The book
Towards Pervasive and Trustworthy Artificial Intelligence
tells the MPAI story in its first 15 months of life: 5 standards produced and 7 projects under way1998.

data.title: Gemini CLI GitHub Actions
data.author: michael-sumner
data.article_summary: Gemini CLI GitHub Actions是一款免费、强大的AI编码辅助工具，适用于团队协作。它可以作为自主代理自动处理常规编码任务，也可以作为按需协作伙伴，接受任务委派。该工具通过触发事件（如新问题或拉取请求）在后台异步工作，利用项目全 context 自动处理任务，如智能问题分类、加速拉取请求审查和按需协作等。它具备企业级安全和控制，支持无凭证认证、细粒度控制和完全透明。现已推出beta版，全球可用，存储库位于google-github-actions/run-gemini-cli。用户可自定义工作流并贡献代码，免费配额丰富，支持Google AI Studio及Vertex AI等。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Google Gemini产品及其相关工具（CLI、GitHub Action、API等）的用户体验和功能争议

不同观点：
• **对产品定位和命名混乱的批评**：
  - [thecupisblue] 认为Google在产品定位上缺乏清晰的战略，导致多个相似产品（如Gemini、Jules等）出现自我竞争，用户感到困惑。
  - [artdigital] 和 [gundmc] 同样对"Gemini CLI"的名称表示质疑，认为其主要通过GitHub使用，称为"GitHub Action"更为合适。

• **对功能和用户体验的不满**：
  - [thecupisblue] 指出Gemini的文档分散，API SDK不统一，功能受限且使用繁琐，对普通用户不友好。
  - [grogenaut] 强调Gemini在日历预约、Google文档编辑等基本功能上的不足，认为Google未能在其生态系统中充分利用AI。
  - [PanMan] 认为设置过程复杂，需要Google Cloud项目，不如GitHub的Cursor Bot简便。

• **对产品潜力的认可与期望**：
  - [jtrn] 试图厘清Gemini工具的本质，认为其在GitHub Actions环境中的应用具有潜力，但需要简化理解过程。
  - [turblety] 希望Google能提供更简单的订阅模式，方便开发者使用多种Gemini工具。

• **与其他工具的比较**：
  - [ssalka] 认为Claude Code比Gemini更有效且便宜。
  - [ncrmro] 则表示Copilot Agent在某些场景下表现出色，Gemini需要更具优势才能替代现有工具。

• **对隐私和安全的关注**：
  - [brtkwr] 对Gemini的免费提供表示怀疑，担心隐私问题，尤其在私有/内部仓库中使用时需谨慎。

补充讨论：
• **对特定功能的兴趣**：
  - [elpakal] 仅对PR审查功能感兴趣，显示出用户对具体功能的需求差异。
  
• **对产品改进的建议和实验**：
  - [stillsut] 分享了其在优化开源代码库审查流程上的实验和框架，以应对AI生成PR的质量问题。

争议焦点：
• Google Gemini产品线的定位不清晰、功能分散、用户体验差以及与竞争产品的比较。

44783372.article_content:
Splatshop: Efficiently Editing Large Gaussian Splat Models
Markus Schütz, Christoph Peters, Florian Hahlbohm, Elmar Eisemann, Marcus Magnor, Michael Wimmer.
2025–06 in
Computer Graphics Forum (Proc. HPG)
44, 8.
Official version
Abstract
We present Splatshop, a highly optimized toolbox for interactive editing (selection, deletion, painting, transformation, ...) of 3D Gaussian Splatting models. Utilizing a comprehensive collection of heuristic approaches, we carefully balance between exact and fast rendering to enable precise editing without sacrificing real-time performance. Our experiments confirm that Splatshop achieves these goals for scenes with up to 100 million primitives. We also show how our proposed pipeline can be extended for use with head-mounted displays. As such, Splatshop is the first VR-capable editor for large-scale 3D Gaussian Splatting models and a step towards a “Photoshop for Gaussian Splatting.”

This work has been presented at HPG 2025 on June 24th. The paper has been published on June 21st.

data.author: OsmanDKitay
data.article_summary: AURA（Agent-Usable Resource Assertion）是一个开放协议，旨在使网站变得机器可读，替代脆弱的屏幕抓取和DOM操作。它通过一个声明式的`aura.json` manifest文件，让网站以安全、高效和标准化的API形式向AI代理暴露其功能。核心概念包括Manifest文件（位于`/.well-known/aura.json`）定义网站能力，Capability描述具体操作（如`create_post`），以及动态HTTP头`AURA-State`提供上下文信息。该协议提供了NPM包和参考服务器实现，帮助网站实现AURA兼容，并展示了如何通过AI代理执行网站功能。这将改变AI与网站交互的方式，从猜测性操作转变为声明式交互。

• **支持AURA标准的观点**
  - 提出AURA可以替代脆弱的屏幕抓取和DOM操作，提供更健壮、安全和高效的机器可读层。

AURA: The Protocol for a Machine-Readable Web
AURA (Agent-Usable Resource Assertion)
is an open protocol for making websites understandable and operable by AI agents. It proposes a new standard for AI-web interaction that moves beyond fragile screen scraping and DOM manipulation towards a robust, secure, and efficient machine-readable layer for the internet.
The web was built for human eyes. AURA is a specification for giving it a machine-readable "API".
The Vision: Why AURA?
Current AI agents interact with websites in a brittle and inefficient way:
Screen Scraping:
They "look" at pixels and guess where to click. This is slow, expensive, and breaks with the slightest UI change.
DOM Manipulation:
They parse complex HTML structures, which are inconsistent across sites and change frequently.
Insecurity:
Website owners have no control over what an agent might do.
AURA solves this by allowing websites to
declare their capabilities
in a simple, standardized
aura.json
manifest file.
Instead of an agent guessing how to "create a post," the website explicitly states:
"I have a capability named
create_post
. It's an
HTTP POST
to
/api/posts
and requires
title
and
content
parameters."
This is a fundamental paradigm shift from
imperative guessing
to
declarative interaction
.
Core Concepts
Manifest (
aura.json
):
A file served at
/.well-known/aura.json
that acts as a site's "API documentation" for AI agents. It defines all available resources and capabilities.
Capability:
A single, discrete action an agent can perform (e.g.,
list_posts
,
login
,
update_profile
). Each capability maps to a specific HTTP request.
State (
AURA-State
Header):
A dynamic HTTP header sent by the server with each response, informing the agent about the current context (e.g., is the user authenticated?) and which capabilities are currently available to them.
This Repository
This repository is the
canonical specification for the AURA protocol
. It provides the core building blocks for the AURA ecosystem:
packages/aura-protocol
: The core
@aura/protocol
NPM package, containing TypeScript interfaces and the official JSON Schema for validation.
This is the heart of AURA.
packages/reference-server
: A reference implementation of an AURA-enabled server built with Next.js. Use this to understand how to make your own website AURA-compliant.
packages/reference-client
: A minimal, backend-only reference client demonstrating two powerful ways to consume the protocol, without any browser or extension required.
Getting Started: A 5-Minute Demonstration
See the protocol in action.
1. Install Dependencies
From the root of the monorepo, install all necessary dependencies for all packages.
pnpm install
2. Run the Reference Server
The server is a sample website that "speaks" AURA.
#
This will start the server (usually on http://localhost:3000)
pnpm --filter aura-reference-server dev
You can now visit
http://localhost:3000/.well-known/aura.json
in your browser to see the manifest.
3. Run the Reference Agent
This simple agent uses an LLM to understand a prompt and execute a capability on the server.
First, create a
.env
file inside the
packages/reference-client
directory and add your OpenAI API key.
OPENAI_API_KEY="sk-..."
Then, run the agent with a URL and a prompt:
#
(In a new terminal)
pnpm --filter aura-reference-client agent -- http://localhost:3000
"
list all the blog posts
"
Observe how the agent fetches the manifest, plans its action, and executes the list_posts capability directly.
4. Run the Crawler (The Big Vision)
This script demonstrates how a search engine could index an AURA-enabled site, understanding its functions, not just its content.
#
In the client directory
pnpm --filter aura-reference-client crawler -- http://localhost:3000
The output shows a structured JSON object representing the site's capabilities. This is the future of search: indexing acti

data.article_summary: 艺术史学家Gergely Barki在观看电影《精灵鼠小弟》时，意外发现匈牙利先锋派画家Róbert Berény的失踪已久的画作《Sleeping Lady with Black Vase》被用作道具。这幅画自1920年代消失后，一直下落不明。Barki通过多封电子邮件联系到电影制作方，得知画作被前任布景设计师从古董店购得，之后卖给私人收藏家。这幅画将于12月13日在布达佩斯拍卖，起拍价约为11万欧元。Berény曾是战前先锋艺术团体“八人组”的领袖，后因政治原因逃亡柏林，其作品因历史动荡而四散流失。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Berény的画作《Sleeping Lady with Black Vase》的历史背景、所有权变迁及其现状

不同观点：
• evaXhill认为这幅画具有重要的历史背景，对它最终流入私人收藏感到遗憾。他提到Berény在第一次世界大战后从柏林返回布达佩斯，而该画作曾在1928年于恩斯特博物馆展出，后来被卖出。evaXhill推测买家可能是犹太人，并在二战期间或之前离开了匈牙利。他强调该画作具有重要历史意义，且是Berény的优秀作品之一，对其现状表示惋惜。

• cafard没有直接讨论画作本身，而是对传闻中Berény与Anastasia的绯闻提出讽刺性评论，暗示某些读者可能会对此类八卦消息一笑而过，而不是深入了解画作本身的艺术和历史价值。这表明他对讨论名人私生活的倾向有所不满。

• j-kent则对画作的重现和即将被拍卖感到高兴，认为这是“人文领域的胜利”。他的观点与evaXhill形成鲜明对比，认为画作进入私人收藏并通过拍卖被重新发现是一个积极的事件，而没有关注其历史背景和可能的遗憾。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于对艺术品流入私人收藏的态度。evaXhill对此表示遗憾，认为具有历史意义的艺术品应该被公开展示，而j-kent则对此表示欢迎，认为拍卖是艺术品重见天日的机会。
• cafard的评论引入了一个与主讨论点无关的八卦话题，暗示对讨论名人私生活的倾向，这在一定程度上偏离了对画作本身的讨论。

A scene from the children’s film Stuart Little with Robert Bereny’s long-lost painting hanging in the background.
A scene from the children’s film Stuart Little with Robert Bereny’s long-lost painting hanging in the background.
Hungary
This article is more than
10 years old
Stuart Little leads art historian to long-lost Hungarian masterpiece
This article is more than 10 years old
Researcher spots Sleeping Lady with Black Vase by Robert Bereny being used as a prop in Hollywood children’s movie
Agence France-Presse in Budapest
Thu 27 Nov 2014 13.02 EST
Last modified on Wed 19 Oct 2022 10.29 EDT
Share
A long-lost avant garde painting has returned to
Hungary
after nine decades thanks to a sharp-eyed art historian, who spotted it being used as a prop in the Hollywood film Stuart Little.
Gergely Barki, 43, a researcher at Hungary’s national gallery in Budapest, noticed Sleeping Lady with Black Vase by Róbert Berény as he watched television with his daughter Lola in 2009.
“I couldn’t believe my eyes when I saw Bereny’s long-lost masterpiece on the wall behind Hugh Laurie. I nearly dropped Lola from my lap,” said Barki. “A researcher can never take his eyes off the job, even when watching Christmas movies at home.”
The painting disappeared in the 1920s, but Barki recognised it immediately even though he had only seen a faded black-and-white photo from an exhibition in 1928.
The big-eyed children: the extraordinary story of an epic art fraud
Read more
He sent a flurry of emails to staff at the film’s makers, Sony Pictures and Columbia Pictures, and received a reply from a former set designer on the film – two years later.
“She said the picture had been hanging on her wall,” Barki said.
“She had snapped it up for next to nothing in an antiques shop in Pasadena, California, thinking its avant garde elegance was perfect for Stuart Little’s living room.”
After leaving Sony, she sold the painting to a private collector who has now brought the picture to Budapest for sale by auction.
Berény, the leader of a pre-first world war avant garde movement called the Group of Eights, fled to Berlin in 1920 after designing recruitment posters for Hungary’s short-lived communist revolution in 1919.
In the German capital, he had a romance with the actor Marlene Dietrich, and – according to Barki – is also rumoured to have had a fling with Anastasia, the mysterious daughter of Russia’s last tsar, Nicholas II.
Berény’s painting will be sold on 13 December, with a starting price of around €110,000 (£87,000), staff at the Virag Judit auction house said.
According to Barki, the buyer at the 1928 exhibition, who was possibly Jewish, is likely to have left Hungary before or during the second world war.
“After the wars, revolutions and tumult of the 20th century, many Hungarian masterpieces are lost, scattered around the world,” he said.
